suppliers.name: Example Web Form Supplier
suppliers.notes: `order_url`, `order_method`, `order_fields` and `reference_regex` used to be shown here, for a path that placed orders automatically. OilWatch does not order: the buying is done by phone or on the supplier's own site and then written down with `record-purchase`, so the keys are gone rather than left as a template nobody should copy. `order_page` is the page a human orders from, not a POST target.

suppliers.name: Example Enquiry Form Supplier
suppliers.notes: quote_request.form names an entry in SUPPLIER_FORMS (oilwatch/form_submit.py), which is what `oilwatch submit-requests` drives. Use {"no_form": true} instead when the supplier has no form: `oilwatch submit-requests --by-email` then writes to this record's own `email`. A supplier with neither a form nor an address is not asked at all - the app never rings a supplier, so its `phone` stays contact data rather than becoming a route.

suppliers.name: Example Benchmark
suppliers.notes: `kind` defaults to "supplier"; "benchmark" marks a figure rather than a company - a UK average, say. Its rows then carry kind: benchmark and order_channel: benchmark, so a consumer can refuse to present it as the winner without reading this note. Leave `kind` out for anything you could actually buy from.
